source: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 18 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 18
knowledgePattern: Separate pointwise order, derivative order and accumulated weighted area
solution:
Let h=f−g. In I, h′(x)≥0 for x≥0 and h(0)≥0. The function cannot decrease below its starting value, so h(x)≥0. I is true.

In II, h(t)≥0 and t≥0 throughout the integration interval. Hence th(t)≥0, so its integral is nonnegative. II is true. The reason is the sign of the integrand, not the fact that t is a linear expression.

For III and IV, take g(x)=0 and f(x)=(x−1)(x−2). The hypothesis really does hold for every x≥0, because ∫0xf(t)dt=x6(2x2−9x+12). The bracket is positive for every real x: its leading coefficient is positive and its discriminant is 81−96=−15.

But f(32)=−14<0, so the conclusion of III fails. III is false.

For IV, ∫02t2f(t)dt=[t55−3t44+2t33]02=325−12+163=−415. This is negative even though the unweighted hypothesis holds everywhere. IV is false.

Only I and II are true, so the answer is F.

hints.title: Subtract the two functions
hints.body: Put h(x)=f(x)−g(x). Rewrite the assumptions and conclusions using h.
hints.recap: The sign of h, the sign of h′ and the integral of h describe different things.
hints.pitfall: Do not differentiate an inequality and assume its direction is preserved.
hints.pause: For I and II, write what the assumptions tell you about h′, h(0), or the sign of th(t).

recall.reminder: A claim about whole functions must hold on the full stated domain.

hints.title: Try a concrete polynomial
hints.body: Test g(x)=0 and f(x)=(x−1)(x−2). Sketch f with its zeros marked, then compare its pointwise sign with the accumulated signed area ∫0xf(t)dt.
hints.recap: An integral records the signed area accumulated so far.
hints.pitfall: The hypothesis about the integral must hold for every x≥0, not just one x.
hints.pause: Check the integral’s sign for all x≥0, then test the proposed pointwise conclusion.

recall.reminder: Expand a polynomial, integrate its powers and apply the limits.

hints.title: Check the weighted area too
hints.body: For the same polynomial, calculate ∫02t2f(t)dt. Compare it with what statement IV would require.
hints.recap: Multiplying by t² changes how much each part of the interval contributes.
hints.pitfall: A varying multiplier is different from multiplying the whole integral by one constant.
hints.pause: Use the exact integral and your earlier checks to decide each statement.

recall.reminder: Evaluate the antiderivative at the upper limit minus its value at the lower limit.
